exposure: COVID-19 case-load in the county on the date of birth
outcome: Quality of perinatal care (measured by Mothers on Respect Index and Mothers Autonomy in Decision Making)
Autonomy in decision-making for perinatal care
cohort: The study included 707 participants from 46 states and the District of Columbia who gave birth in the United States after March 15, 2020.
finding: Increased COVID-19 cases were associated with significantly decreased autonomy in perinatal decision-making, and low-quality perinatal care was more likely among Black, Indigenous, and people of color, those with an obstetrician provider, and those giving birth in a hospital.
cross-section timing: Data collected via online questionnaire from people who gave birth after March 15, 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic.
